substantive_units.result: Constructed and directly replayed an actual n=33,m=143 D2C graph containing the locally saturated RTS bow-tie, proving that this triangle geometry is graph-realizable.
Constructed an actual n=34,m=148 D2C RTS-bow-tie control with the fourth cross pair missing, while the n=33 control has it present. Therefore neither fourth-pair status is universally forced.

Completed an exact uniform graph-level grid: with six coordinate codes and 2<=r,q<=8, equal star multiplicities one and two reject the RTS bow-tie, while multiplicity three is feasible exactly for r>=4 throughout the tested rectangle. This is diagnostic, not an arbitrary-multiplicity theorem.
Found that the actual n=33 RTS control has parity/star block B=21>rq+s=20. This is a literal D2C counterexample to universal exact cancellation; the budgeted-excess theorem survives.
Exact fixed-multiset MaxSAT proves max B=21=rq+s+1 under the smallest saved RTS constraints, independently confirming and quantifying the exact-cancellation failure.
Proved the unconditional quantitative replacement for exact cancellation: epsilon=max(0,B-rq-s)<=min(U,k(q-1))<=min(U,s(q-1)), where k is the number of high-bridge stars.
Fed the new excess bound into the density budget: the branch closes whenever s(2(t+r-q)+s)>=12. Hence every survivor must satisfy q>t+r+floor((s-ceil(12/s))/2), a strongly P1-dominant wedge.
Strengthened the excess bound symmetrically: the centre-spoke P0 nonneighbour requirement gives e(R,S)<=s(r-1), which combines with epsilon<=U to yield epsilon<=max(0,floor(s(r+q-2)/2)).

Compared the symmetric excess cap with D(u,s) and closed the entire exactly-four-centre Q3 antipodal-transversal branch: every such D2C graph satisfies m<=M(n), with at least eleven units of budget slack when r+q>=2.
